text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

- Centre-right Social Democratic Party (PSD) leader Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa, who strengthened his grip on the party at its congress over the weekend, has secured his position until at least the next local elections in December 1997.

- Transport company Tertir seeks business in Mozambique, Angola and Guinea-Bissau. Tertir's chairman, Rodrigo Leite, believes such business will boost the company's share price on Lisbon stock exchange.
- State-owned forests, which represent 25 percent of the Portuguese forest stock, will be managed by a public company.
- A proposal by the European Commission to liberalise the textile industry could mean 20,000 lost jobs in Portugal.
- The so-called "Mateus Plan", which offers incentives to help struggling firms to recover financially, could increase the tax burden in the short term.
- Poor training and preparation are to blame for the poor quality of Portuguese education, a poll shows.
- Turnover of Portuguese car components industry around 500 billion escudos a year.
- Planning Minister Joao Cravinho promises to invest more than 573.9 billion escudos in railway infrastructure until the year 2000, double that invested between 1988 and 1995.
